The Material guidance on the navigation icon and title is consistent across the results.

- **Navigation icon:** The icon is optional and sits on the left edge of the bar. Material's own guide lists three forms: a menu icon that opens a navigation drawer, an up arrow for moving up a hierarchy, and a back arrow for returning to the previous screen (it's aligned on the left of the bar. It can take any of the following forms). The Material page is the primary source here.
- **Title:** The title is also optional. Per a community summary of the guidelines, it tells users which screen, scene, or function they are in (用來告知用戶當前所在的畫面、場景或是功能, Chinese-language source).
- **Back arrow on subpages:** SAP's Fiori Android guide, which extends Material, says a small bar with a left-aligned title suits subpages that need back navigation (used for subpages that require back navigation or close/cancel and multiple actions).
- **Code:** Jetpack Compose's `TopAppBar` has slots for a title, a navigation icon, and actions (slots for a title, navigation icon, and actions). A Slack thread shows the usual pattern of pairing `Icons.Default.ArrowBack` with a title text in that slot (navigationIcon = { Icon(imageVector = Icons.Default.ArrowBack). The Android developer guide covers wiring the navigation icon to a back-navigation callback (This example uses a back arrow for the icon.).

Two caveats: the results mostly cover Material Design 2-era and Compose docs, so check current Material 3 pages for exact spacing or naming. Also, the Material spec says contextual mode swaps the back or menu icon for a close icon (per the Material page's description of contextual bars).

input.query: Apple Human Interface Guidelines navigation bar back button title previous view

content.text:
Yes, it's a common convention. Two major design systems handle it differently, and this screen follows the more common one.

**Android and Material Design (what this screen does).** The top bar has a back arrow on the left, and the text next to it is the title of the screen you're on. The arrow has no label of its own and just means "go back." [Material's top app bar guide](https://material.io/components/app-bars-top) lists three things that can sit in that left spot: a back arrow, an up arrow, or a menu icon. The title says which screen you're on ([summary](https://ithelp.ithome.com.tw/articles/10295351)). [Jetpack Compose's `TopAppBar`](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/compose/components/app-bars) has a slot for the icon and a separate slot for the title. SAP's Fiori guidelines for Android, which build on Material, recommend [this bar with the title on the left for subpages that need a back button](https://www.sap.com/design-system/fiori-design-android/v26-4/components/navigation-and-search/top-app-bar/usage). From memory, not checked today: macOS System Settings also puts back/forward chevrons next to the current pane's name.

**iOS (the reading you expected).** iOS puts the label on the back button itself, and it names the screen you'll go back to. By default it reuses the previous screen's title, so it would read "‹ Home", and the current screen's title sits in the middle of the bar. The [HIG on navigation bars](https://developer-mdn.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/components/navigation-and-search/navigation-bars) covers the design side, and [UIKit's `backButtonTitle`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uinavigationitem/backbuttontitle.md) explains where the default label comes from.

So "‹ Print history" is correct by the Material convention. JusPrin uses the same pattern elsewhere: the All settings panel in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` has an icon button back to the chat, then the panel's own title in bold.

Your confusion has a real cause, though. In your screenshot, the title starts right after the chevron with nothing between them. That makes it read like one button labelled "Print history," which is the iOS reading. Material avoids that because the arrow is a full-size icon button with its own hover area, and the title is plain text clearly apart from it. If you want this screen to be unambiguous, there are two ways to do it:
- Make the arrow look like a separate icon button: a bigger hit area, its own hover fill, and more space before the title.
- Switch to the iOS style: "‹ Home" on the left and "Print history" as the page title.

I haven't changed anything. This is only a reading of the screen and the conventions.
No matter what style we follow, at least we want to be consistent within our own app, right? Check to see if the consistency is there in your app.

input.recap: JusPrin's back controls are not consistent. Six screens use three styles: an arrow with the current page's title, an arrow with the word "Back", and an arrow with the name of the page you return to. I found this by reading the code. I didn't open each screen in the app, and nothing has changed.
input.ask: Which convention should every back control follow?

content.text:
No, the app isn't consistent. It has six back controls at the top of a screen or pane, and they use three different styles. One of them is the style you expected. I checked this by reading the code, not by opening each screen, so the wording below is what the code draws.

| Where | What the person sees | Style |
|---|---|---|
| Print history (from Home or a project) | ‹ icon, then "Print history" | Arrow + current page's title |
| A chat in the AI pane | ‹ icon, then the chat's title | Arrow + current page's title |
| All settings in the AI pane | ‹ icon, then "All settings" | Arrow + current page's title |
| Printer setup / connecting conversation | "‹ Back" text link, no title | Arrow + the word "Back" |
| Filament settings help conversation | "‹ Back" text link, no title. The screen-reader name says "Back to Prepare" or "Back to Preview", but that text isn't shown | Arrow + the word "Back" |
| Project pane › Details, and › Version history | "‹ Project", with "Details" or "Version history" on the line below | Arrow + where it goes (iOS style) |

A seventh case mixes two styles. When you connect an AI tool from the Agent setup screens, the arrow and the screen's title form one button, so clicking "‹ Claude Desktop" takes you back to the list. It reads like a destination but shows the current page. That's the same thing that confused you on Print history. The code comment says this was deliberate ([SetupLocalTool.tsx:5](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupLocalTool.tsx:5)).

I left out the "Back" buttons that move you through the steps of a form, in first-run onboarding and the add-printer form. Those step back within the same screen and aren't page navigation.

The design docs don't settle this either. `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` describes the All settings header as an icon button back to the chat plus the panel's title. It says nothing about back controls in general.

**Decision needed: which back-control style should the whole app use?** It's your call because it changes the visible wording on six screens, and the design boards would need updating before the code. Option one is to name the destination: "‹ Home", "‹ Chats", "‹ Chat", "‹ Prepare", with the current page's title on its own line or clearly apart from the arrow. That answers the question you had: the words say where the arrow goes. Most of the data is already there. The project pane already does this, and the printer and filament conversations already know "Back to Prepare" or "Back to Preview". The cost is room in the narrow AI pane, where a chat header already holds the title, New chat, a menu, and the pane toggle. The chat title would likely need its own line. Option two is the arrow plus the current page's title, the Android convention three screens already use. It's cheaper in narrow panes. It needs titles added to the printer and filament conversations, and the project pane rewritten. It also keeps the ambiguity you ran into, unless the arrow becomes a clearly separate button with its own hover area and space before the title. My pick is option one, because it's the one you read correctly without being told the convention. Which should it be?

I don't have a strong opinion. Do some research on how this is typically done for a desktop app like ours. Also, ideally, we want to include the home page into the same consistent navigation style, right?

input.recap: On desktop, the common pattern is an arrow-only back button at the top left followed by the current screen's title, with the destination in the tooltip. I found that the project screen's "‹ Home" button teaches the opposite reading, which explains how Print history confused you. Nothing has changed in the app or the design boards.
input.ask: Adopt the desktop convention across the app, Home included?

content.text:
On desktop apps, the usual pattern is a back button that's just an arrow, at the top left, followed by the title of the screen you're on. Where the arrow goes shows only in its tooltip. That's how Print history already works. The research also explains why it confused you. Every time you open a project, the button you use to leave says "‹ Home", which names where it goes. So you've learned to read the text next to an arrow as its destination.

**What the desktop platforms do**
- **Windows:** Microsoft puts the back button in the [upper-left corner, to the left of the page title](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/design/basics/titlebar-design). The button is just a back glyph, with no text label. Its [navigation history guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/WINDOWS/APPS/develop/ui/navigation/navigation-history-and-backwards-navigation) says the same. Microsoft also says to [use breadcrumbs only for deep hierarchies, not for two levels](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/design/controls/breadcrumbbar).
- **macOS:** Apple says [macOS has no navigation bar](https://developer-mdn.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/components/navigation-and-search/navigation-bars). Mac apps use a Back button in the toolbar, and the title describes the current window or view ([toolbars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toolbars.md)). System Settings has [back and forward arrows](https://support.apple.com/is-is/guide/mac-help/mchldfdf4f86/14.0/mac/14.0) next to the name of the pane you're in.
- **Linux (GNOME):** The header bar shows [the current page's title](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1.5/class.HeaderBar.html) with a back button that's just an arrow. The destination page's title is used only as the button's [tooltip and screen-reader name](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/main/method.NavigationPage.set_title.html).
- **Naming the destination** ("‹ Home") is the iOS phone convention. John Gruber [argues for it](https://daringfireball.net/linked/2011/10/25/back-button). GNOME [decided against it](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/merge_requests/951), because keeping the destination name correct is hard when a screen can be reached from several places. JusPrin has that exact problem: Print history opens from Home or from a project.
- **Getting back to Home from a document:** Photoshop uses a [Home icon in the upper left](https://helpx.adobe.com/sg/photoshop/desktop/get-started/learn-the-basics/homescreen-overview.html). That's a "go Home" button, not a "back" button. OrcaSlicer, the app JusPrin is forked from, has Home as a tab beside Prepare and Preview. JusPrin hides that tab strip.

**Home in the same scheme.** I agree it should be included, and today it's a fourth style: the Home header reads "JusPrin › Home", a breadcrumb trail. Under the desktop convention, my proposal would be:
- Home shows only its title, "Home", with no arrow and no "JusPrin ›" in front. The app's name is already in the window and the Dock.
- Every screen below Home gets the same arrow-only button at the top left, then its own title. The tooltip and screen-reader name say where the button goes ("Back to Home", "Back to chats").
- The arrow must look like a separate button, with its own hover fill and a clear gap before the title. On Print history the gap is missing, and that's part of why it read as one label.
- The project screen's "‹ Home" becomes a Home icon, as in Photoshop, because opening a 3MF from Finder never went through Home. "Back" isn't accurate there, but "go Home" always is.

Six places would change: the project screen's Home button, the Home header, the printer setup and filament help conversations (an arrow and a title instead of "‹ Back"), the project pane's Details and Version history views, and the AI-tool setup screens. Print history, the chat header and All settings already match.

This changes my earlier pick. Last time I recommended naming the destination because it matched how you read the screen. The research shows that reading comes from the project screen's "‹ Home" button rather than from any desktop convention. Naming the destination would mean changing seven places instead of six, and a label like "‹ Prepare" would have to be computed for every way someone can reach a screen. All of this is a proposal. If you agree, the design boards get updated first, then the code.
Don't update all the boards for now. Show me 2 mock-ups for desktop convention here or on canvas and I can have a visual to review

preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
## screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture.md

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].
## capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff.md

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.

content.text:
I've sent you three images that make up the two mock-ups. In both, the rule is: Home has no back button, and every screen below it has an outlined arrow button at the top left followed by that screen's own title.

**Mock-up 1, Home and Print history.** I made both images by loading the app's real Home page with sample data and changing only the headers.
- **Home:** the header shows only the JusPrin logo. "› Home" is gone, so it no longer reads as a trail of pages. Everything else is the real page. The project cards have no pictures because my sample projects have none.
- **Print history:** the arrow is now a separate button with an outline. The image shows it hovered, with its tooltip "Back to Home". The title "Print history" stands apart from the button.

**Mock-up 2, the project screen.** This one is drawn, not rendered from the app, because the header and left panel are native windows. It uses the design tokens, the app's font, and strings from the approved "Festival arrow headband" canvas board. The 3D view is a placeholder.
- **Top left:** a house button that goes to Home, replacing today's "‹ Home". The house icon isn't in the app's icon set yet, so it would be a new icon.
- **Left panel, Version history:** the arrow button sits beside "Version history" on one row. Today the panel shows "‹ Project" with the view's title on a second line.
- **AI panel:** the chat header uses the same outlined arrow beside the chat's title.
- **Tooltips:** they'd be "Home", "Back to Project" and "Back to chats". I left them out of the picture because, drawn all at once, they covered the tabs and the setup summary.

**What a first-time reader made of them.** I gave the three images, with no other context, to a separate agent playing a first-time user.
- **Print history:** it was sure the arrow goes to Home, because of the tooltip.
- **The house button:** it was fairly sure this goes to Home, about 85%.
- **The two arrows inside the project screen:** it was much less sure. It said about 60% that the Version history arrow returns to the Project tab, and thought it might leave the project instead. For the chat arrow it said about 65% that it goes to a chat list.

That points at a real weakness. The arrows look identical, and you only learn where one goes by hovering over it. The reader also noticed that the way to Home is an arrow on Print history but a house on the project screen, and wondered whether the two mean the same thing.

Two adjustments would deal with that, and both are proposals. One is to put the house button on Print history too, wherever Home is the destination. The other is to keep arrows only for going back inside a panel, and accept that the destination shows only in the tooltip, as every desktop platform does.

I haven't changed the app or the canvas boards.

You need to consider if the proposals work for other screens. For example, if we use a house button, doesn't mean that every screen would sort of have its own icon that's very recognizable. The proposal such as to keep arrows only for going back inside the piano. Doesn't mean that arrows will not play a role on a top net and in that case when things such as printer chat is open. What can we use to make it go back to the previous page?

Primary Request and Intent: - First question: is it a convention that the label next to a back arrow ("‹ Print history") names the current page rather than the destination? This came up on JusPrin's Print history screen, opened from Home. - Second request: check whether JusPrin is consistent about its back-arrow style. - Third request: research how desktop apps typically do this, and include the Home page in the same consistent navigation style. The user had no strong opinion. - Latest request (verbatim): "Don't update all the boards for now. Show me 2 mock-ups for desktop convention here or on canvas and I can have a visual to review". The design boards and canvas must NOT be updated. Only the mock-ups are wanted, for visual review. 2. result.output:
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in the design artifacts, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
- Setup card (the design system's `PinnedSetupCard`; the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", decided 2026-10-26): the band docked under the chat header, the one place in the Agent pane that is always now. Two parts. Above a 1 DIP `border.subtle` rule, the words someone wrote: the person's purpose in Body Bold, wrapping to two lines and then clipped (the whole of it in the tooltip), and the agent's plan headline in Body Small, `text.primary`; each is present only once written, and with neither the section and its rule are absent, with nothing standing in for them (not the preset name, not the project name, not a hint). Below the rule, OrcaSlicer's facts: the process and first filament presets with "N settings changed" (the project's differences from the presets and the objects' own settings) in Body Small, `text.secondary`, wrapping to two lines and then clipped like the purpose (decided 2026-10-26: at the pane's default width a Bambu preset name with a count overflows one line), and the "All settings" Button/Link, in Body Small Bold, on its first line's baseline; then the time, material and plate figures in Body Small Bold, or the one line that stands in for them ("Not sliced yet" with a Compute estimates link, "Time & material estimates recomputing…"). The eyebrow is "Setup summary" in Label Bold, `action.primary`; the only state beside it is "Agent working". A saved chat's card is the same card in `text.secondary` with the eyebrow "Earlier setup" or "Saved sliced snapshot", a quiet state such as "Saved Oct 3, 10:42" and a footnote line.
- Setup card warnings: a warning is only an annotation of the one line it contradicts, drawn directly under it, one per line: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` beside Body Small text in `text.primary`. The three in use: what moved since the plan was recorded, in words the person and the model both read ("Filament changed to Generic ABS by hand", "Wall loops changed to 5 by hand", "Rename Object undone by hand", "An earlier model version was restored"; "Plan needs another look" when the host gave no reason), with a Check plan link that sends "Check the plan against what changed." in the person's name, under the plan (the app's mark after an edit that was not the agent's, cleared only by the agent recording the plan again; a setup switch stays the named reason over the setting edits after it), "Printer last reported <material>" under the presets, and "Previous estimates · not current" with a Recompute link under the estimates. A warning that names no line of the card is not the card's: print issues belong to the canvas and the chat; a mismatch between the selection and the connected machine (its nozzle, its model, what it has loaded) belongs to the chat and to the send dialog, never to the chip (see Header chip). Moments of change ("Updated", the last step with Undo, an estimate before and after, an edit by hand, "Confirmed") are the timeline rows', never the card's.
- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate and warning glyphs sit inside a row of Label text, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.
- Agent message box: one box with the `medium` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke, and `component.composer` insets (8 DIP padding, 4 DIP between staged files, the field, and the toolbar). The field is Body with a 4 DIP inset; it grows a line at a time up to `component.composer.maxLines` (8) and then scrolls, while the toolbar stays visible: the 32 DIP + icon button on the left, Send (`button.primarySmall`, 28 DIP) or Stop (`button.secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) on the right. While the field has the focus the whole box carries the 2 DIP `border.focus` ring. In the app, each + menu choice opens the operating system's file dialog through the host, filtered to that kind. The printer chat's + menu offers only Photo or image and Document (PDF), since it has no project for a 3D model to go into. After + come the model and thinking pickers (`button.picker`: 24 DIP, Label, a chevron), which open upward menus no narrower than `component.popover.width`: the model menu lists each set-up provider's models under the provider's name when there is more than one (a provider is added from the Agent settings); the thinking menu lists only the levels the chosen model accepts and is left out when it accepts none. A choice belongs to the chat and applies from its next turn. When the full labels do not fit beside + and Send (the composer measures them, so this follows the labels, not a breakpoint), the thinking picker drops "Thinking:" and shows the level alone; if that still does not fit, the model's name is cut with an ellipsis. Both keep their full name as the accessible name and the tooltip. A model menu of more than 12 models opens with the focus in a Field/Search (`component.fieldSearch`: 38 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that becomes 2 DIP `border.strong` with the focus) inset 8 DIP from the menu's sides; the menu is then `component.popover.width` wide and its rows scroll under the field. Typing filters on the model or provider name, ignoring case, the first match carries the menu-row hover fill, Up and Down move it, Enter picks it, and Escape clears the field before it closes the menu. A provider with more than 12 models shows its count beside its name while nothing is typed.
- All settings panel (the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", the four "All settings" boards): opened from the "All settings" link at the end of the setup card's presets line, it takes the Agent pane's place under a header of the compact icon button back to the chat, the title in Body Bold and the pane's own toggle. A "Showing" row holds the design system's Select (`component.select`: 26 DIP, `small` radius, Body text, a 16 DIP chevron, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that strengthens on hover and becomes the focus ring when open; its menu is the Menu/Popover under its left edge, as wide as the field) listing the whole project, each plate when there are two or more, and each object; it follows the selection in the 3D view. Under it a Field/Search ("Search settings") beside an All / Changed Segmented Control. The presets in use sit in a `surface.subtle` box with the `medium` radius, each filament slot with its Swatch (`component.swatch`, 24 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke). Groups are OrcaSlicer's own pages (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial, Others, then Filament and Printer) with a 32 DIP header row (16 DIP chevron, Body Small Bold name, Label summary at the right) and rows indented 24 DIP: Body Small name and value on a 28 DIP line, a changed value in Body Small Bold with "Preset: …" in Metadata under it. Two or three filament slots stand side by side, one column per slot; more than three go through a slot picker, one at a time. The host reads the whole table in one message (`settings_catalog`, the `all_settings` capability). Only one object's view has anything to press: a Button/Link at the end of a row's note, under the value, where the table marks one — "Use project value" under a setting the object, a part, a modifier or a height range sets itself (not a range's own layer height or filament, which define it), and "Remove" under its support blockers or enforcers. Each press is one OrcaSlicer undo step of the person's, named for what it did, and the panel redraws from the host's next table (`settings_action`, the `settings_actions` capability).
- Shared progress track: 4 DIP from `component.progress.height`; PrinterCard and Agent activity use this role rather than owning separate track heights.
- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
- Icon button: 32×32 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius (`component.button.icon`).
- Compact icon target: 26×26 DIP (`component.button.iconCompact`), only for the canvas tool strip and the reset button in a form row, which stands at the field's height.
- Link button: 26 DIP high, 4 DIP horizontal padding, Label Bold in `action.primary`, underlined on hover (`component.button.link`).
- Segmented control: a 30 DIP `surface.subtle` track with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` border and 2 DIP padding, holding 24 DIP segments in Label; the chosen one is `action.primary` (`component.segmented`).
- Tooltip: 24 DIP high, 4×8 DIP padding, Metadata, inverse (`text.primary` fill, `surface.canvas` text) with the subtle elevation (`component.tooltip`). Native tooltips are the operating system's own.
- Header chip: 28 DIP high, `chip` radius (`component.chip`). The chip states the selection: the printer profile the project will be sliced for, its nozzle, the project's filaments. It may qualify that statement, and must, when the plain statement would mislead; the qualification is about the selection itself, comes from OrcaSlicer's own state, and holds regardless of what the chat says. The chip makes no claim about the physical machine: what is loaded, which plate is on, which nozzle is fitted, whether it is connected or busy. Those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row, and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip. (Kenneth, 2026-09-06, restated 2026-10-28: the September rule "the chip states facts and never warns" was about the chat steering the chip and about mismatches with the connected machine; it was not about the selection.) Four tests for any mark proposed for the chip:
  1. Is it about the selection or about the machine? Machine means not on the chip.
  2. Would the chip's plain text mislead without it? If not, it is a warning, and warnings go to the chat.
  3. Does it come from OrcaSlicer's preset state, or from an observation or a judgement? Observations and judgements go to the chat.
  4. Can the chat create or clear it? If yes, it is not the chip's.

  The one mark in use passes all four. Its printer half is marked while the selected printer profile is not one of the person's named printers and not OrcaSlicer's placeholder (`Printers::printer_from_file`), which is what opening a 3MF saved for another printer leaves selected: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` takes the printer glyph's place, the label reads "<model> · <nozzle> · from the file" in `text.primary`, and the tooltip names the file. The chip's menu then opens with that printer and the Body Small line "From the file · not one of your printers", a row that cannot be pressed; every other row is the stock menu. Nothing is stored: the mark goes when a named printer is selected, from the menu or by the agent. Decided 2026-10-28; boards 1 to 5 of "File for another printer" on the canvas's Printer & Material Settings page.
- Reply choice (Chat/Reply Choice): drawn as a reply the person could send, not as an app control. 28 DIP high with `component.replyChip` padding, the `full` radius (the one capsule control), Body `text.primary` on `surface.subtle` (the person's own bubble) with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke; hover and pressed go to `surface.selected`, never `action.primary`. A tapped choice is sent as the person's bubble in the same tint and words.
- Jump to latest (Chat/Jump to latest; the "JusPrin v2" canvas, Agent UI page, "Chat scrolling", decided 2026-10-28): the one icon button with the `full` radius, 32 DIP (`button.icon` size; `full` is 14 DIP, so it is nearly round with short flat sides, kept as drawn by Kenneth on 2026-10-28, 16 DIP Lucide `arrow-down` in `text.primary`) on `surface.canvas` with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke and `elevation.subtle`, centred 8 DIP above the composer over the thread's bottom edge; hover `surface.subtle`, pressed `surface.selected`. It is shown only while the thread's bottom is out of view, with no label and no count, and pressing it scrolls to the bottom and follows again. The thread follows new content while the person is at the bottom, including when the composer grows; a scroll up holds the view, and answers and the app's own turns never move it; any message of the person's (typed, a reply choice, Ask AI) scrolls to the bottom and follows again.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the boards on the canvas's Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Agent-pane collapse: an icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

input.recap: The house-button idea doesn't hold up. Print history, the printer chat and the filament chat each go back to different screens depending on where they were opened. A revised rule uses one arrow everywhere, where its position says what it leaves. Nothing has been changed or drawn yet.
input.ask: Should I draw the printer chat and project screen with the revised arrows and re-run the first-time-reader check?

content.text:
You're right on both counts. A house icon for Home would push us toward an icon for every destination, and that doesn't scale. The arrow also can't be kept to panels, because the printer chat already uses it at the top of the window. I've dropped the house idea. What follows is a revised proposal: one arrow everywhere, where its position tells you what it leaves.

**Why the house doesn't work.** Several screens go back to different places depending on where you opened them, so no single icon can name the destination:
- **Print history** opens from Home, and also from inside a project. Opened from a project, its Back returns to the project (`ShellController.cpp:1723`).
- **The printer chat** (the chat for adding or connecting a printer) returns to Home, Prepare or Preview, whichever you opened it from. Prepare is the editing view and Preview the sliced view.
- **The filament chat** returns to Prepare or Preview. The app already builds its accessible name, "Back to Prepare" or "Back to Preview", from where it was opened.

**What the top bar looks like when the printer chat is open.** When either the printer chat or the filament chat opens, the app hides the window header, the left panel and the AI panel, and the chat fills the whole window. The chat's own header becomes the top bar, with "‹ Back" at its top left. So that arrow already does the same job as the project screen's "‹ Home": it leaves the whole screen.

**Revised proposal (not agreed).** Use one control everywhere, the outlined arrow button. It leaves the view it sits in and goes back to the one underneath. Where it sits says what it leaves:
- **Top left of the window** (the window header, or a chat that fills the window): it leaves the screen.
  - The project screen goes to Home.
  - Print history goes to Home or the project.
  - The printer chat goes to Home, Prepare or Preview.
  - The filament chat goes to Prepare or Preview.
  - Home has no arrow.
- **Top left of a panel:** it changes what that panel shows and never leaves the screen. A chat goes back to the chat list, All settings goes back to the chat, and Version history goes back to the Project tab.
- **First row of a header menu:** it returns from a sub-list to the menu's first page. The printer and filament menus already work this way.

Next to each arrow sits the title of the view you're on. The tooltip and the screen-reader name say where it goes, worked out from where the view was opened, as the filament chat already does.

**Two gaps to settle:**
- **No titles yet.** Today the printer chat and the project screen have no title beside the arrow. The printer chat could show something like "Add a printer" or the printer's name. The project screen could show the project name, or just the arrow before the printer and filament selector.
- **Panel arrows may still read as leaving.** The first-time reader was only 60 to 65% sure the panel arrows stay inside the project. On the project screen there would be three identical arrows: one for the window and one in each panel. If a new check still finds them confusing, the fallback is to label panel arrows with their destination, as "‹ Project" and "‹ Chats". That's what the left panel already does today. Window-level arrows would stay arrow plus title.

I haven't changed the app or the canvas boards.

A few thoughts that you need to validate against your own knowledge base and the information you can gather online. One. Maybe we can use different styles of arrows that are very distinguished from each other from each other to between the window and the panel so that we built the a pattern for our users to know how the behavior differs between these two. And two Two, the current page title, should it be centered on the line line or a line to the left that's closer to the arrow. If the title is centered to the line, it won't be confused as what the error leads to, right? However, I can see the problem that in the channel, uh in the panel, such as the chat panel. having the title centered on the header line does not even make sense because of the limited space.

The official Android guidance draws the distinction mainly by how many actions a screen needs. Small (left-aligned) is for screens without much navigation or actions, while center-aligned suits screens with a single primary action. Small: For screens that don't require a lot of navigation or actions. Center aligned: For screens that have a single, primary action. Apart from the title position, the two are otherwise the same. The center aligned top app bar is essentially the same as the small app bar, though the title is centered within the component.

Other sources give more specific usage examples:
- A third-party Jetpack Compose guide suggests small bars for simple titled screens such as settings, and center-aligned bars for screens with navigation or actions, such as a details screen with a back button. (knockzyteam.blogspot.com)

I didn't find a source covering Material 3's own design-site guidance directly, so the Android developer docs are the most authoritative result here.

input.recap: I checked both ideas against the Windows, macOS, GNOME and Material guidelines. The platforms tell temporary layers apart from back steps by using a close X, not a second arrow shape. Windows and macOS put the title on the left, next to the back button. Nothing has been drawn or changed.
input.ask: Should I draw mock-ups with the close X and both arrow styles for a first-time-reader test?

content.text:
Short version: the platform guidelines back your second idea, a title kept to the left, more than they back centering. For your first idea they use a different tool. They don't give window and panel two arrow shapes; they give a temporary layer a close X instead of an arrow.

**Idea 1: a different arrow for the window and for panels**

- **What I found.** None of the guidelines I checked tells two "back" actions apart by the shape of the arrow. Windows uses a plain arrow (←) and macOS uses a chevron (‹), but each platform uses its one glyph everywhere. I found no research showing people learn that ← and ‹ go to different places. Icon studies at Nielsen Norman Group (a usability research firm) found that many icons aren't recognized at all. My hypothesis is that a difference this small would go unnoticed, but I haven't seen a test of that.
- **What the platforms do instead.** Material Design, Flutter and SAP's Android guidelines all mark a temporary full-screen layer with a close X, not a back arrow. A back arrow appears only for steps deeper inside that layer. The difference carries meaning: X means "put this away and go back to what's underneath", while the arrow means "go up a level".
- **How that fits JusPrin.** Our design doc already calls the printer chat and the filament chat a "temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace". The printer chat even asks you to confirm before you close it with an unsent message. They fit the close-X pattern exactly.

Proposal (not agreed), in three tiers:
- **Close X** for the printer chat and the filament chat.
- **The outlined arrow** in the window header, for the project screen and Print history.
- **A smaller arrow in a panel's own header**, for the chat list, All settings and Version history. Here the difference would come from size and from which header the arrow sits in, not from a new glyph.

One risk: on Windows, an X at the top right would sit right under the window's own close button, so ours belongs at the top left. If you still want two arrow shapes, the arrow for the window and the chevron for panels is cheap to try. It should go through the same first-time-reader check before we commit to it.

**Idea 2: center the title, or put it next to the arrow**

- **Centered:** iOS centers the title, because its back button carries the previous screen's name and centering keeps the two apart. GNOME's header bars also center the title, and Material offers a centered version for simple screens.
- **Left, next to the button:** Windows puts the title 16 px to the right of the back button. macOS puts the back controls at the leading (left) edge with the view title after them. Material's default bar also puts the title on the left.
- **Why the left still works.** The confusion you hit on Print history didn't come from the title being on the left. It came from the arrow being a bare glyph with no border, right next to bold text, so "‹ Print history" read as one link. An outlined button with a gap fixes that, as in the Print history mock-up I sent.
- **The problem in panels.** You're right that centering breaks down there. The AI panel can be as narrow as 320 px, and the chat header has one button on the left and three on the right, so a centered title would either sit off-center or lose room. Chat titles are long and already get cut off.

**My pick (proposal):** keep the title on the left, beside a visibly separate button, everywhere. That matches Windows and macOS, it fits the panels, and it means one rule for every screen.

Sources:
- [Android: app bars](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/compose/components/app-bars)
- [Close vs. up icon (quoting Material)](https://kiwix.lema.org/stackoverflow.com_en_all_2023-11/questions/53644705/when-to-use-close-vs-up-navigation-back-icon-in-screens)
- [Flutter fullscreenDialog](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/MaterialPage/fullscreenDialog.html)

content.text:
Splitting the arrows into two styles helped. The weak spot is now the project screen's window arrow, which has no title beside it. These figures come from a single first-time reader with no tooltips, so they're a direction, not proof.

The three mock-ups:
- **Printer chat:** an outlined X at the top left of the window, then "Add a printer". That's the text of the existing menu command, without its "…".
- **Project screen:** the window arrow is an outlined square button with a straight arrow (←). The arrows in the left panel and the AI panel are small chevrons (‹) with no outline.
- **Print history:** the same outlined window arrow, then "Print history".

What the reader expected each control to do:

| Control | Reader expected | Sure | Last time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Print history arrow | Back to Home | 90% | about 95%, but that image showed the tooltip |
| Project screen's window arrow | Leave the project for Home | 70% | 85%, as a house icon |
| Chevron by "Version history" | Back one step inside the Project tab | 80% | 60% |
| Chevron by the chat title | Back to the chat list | 75% | 65% |
| Printer chat X | Cancel and go back to the project | 75% | (new) |

**What worked.** Both panel chevrons scored higher than the matching outlined arrows did last time. The reader also took the X and the arrow to mean different things: X discards, the arrow keeps your work and goes back. That's the difference we want. For unsent text, the reader expected the X to throw it away and wasn't sure whether it would warn first. The printer chat already asks for confirmation before closing with an unsent message.

**What didn't:**
- **The window arrow has no title.** Every other arrow has the current view's name beside it. This one has nothing, so the reader had no clue where it goes, and briefly wondered whether it was Undo. The reader called it "the dangerous one". It sits about 100 px from the two panel chevrons, and reaching for it to get out of Version history would leave the project. My proposal is to put the project name beside it ("Festival arrow headband"). Then it follows the same rule as Print history.
- **"‹ Version history" partly read as a destination.** The reader went 65/35 for it naming the current view. Without an outline, the chevron runs into the text, which is the same reading that started this whole discussion. A wider gap, or a lighter chevron than the title, might fix it. I haven't tested either.
- **The X at the top left** reminded the reader of the macOS button that closes a window. In the real app the window's title bar sits above this row, so the two wouldn't touch. Still, a text button such as "Close" would remove the doubt on both macOS and Windows. Moving it to the top right would put it under the Windows close button.

content.text:
The project name helped. A new first-time reader was more sure of every control than the last one. The one doubt left is whether leaving the project saves your work, and the app already handles that. Each run is a single reader with no tooltips, so treat the numbers as a direction, not proof.

How sure each reader was about where a control goes:

| Control | 1st reader | 2nd reader | Now, with name |
|---|---|---|---|
| Print history arrow | 95%, with tooltip | 90% | 90% |
| Project screen's window arrow | 85%, house icon | 70%, no name | 75% |
| Chevron by "Version history" | 60%, outlined arrow | 80% | 85% |
| Chevron by the chat title | 65%, outlined arrow | 75% | 80% |
| Printer chat X | (not shown) | 75% | 80% that it cancels; 60% that it returns to the project |

**What's left:**
- **Saving when you leave a project.** The reader was 75% sure the arrow leads back to the project cards, but only 40% sure what happens to the project on the way. In the app today, going Home just switches to the Home screen. The project stays open behind it, and the app autosaves it. The code also sets the window's title bar to the name plus the save state, for example "Festival arrow headband — Saved". So the worry has a real answer the screen doesn't show. One way to show it (a proposal) is to put "Saved" in smaller grey text after the project name in the header.
- **The name repeats the title bar.** Because the title bar already shows the project name, the name in our header appears twice on screen. The duplicate buys a consistent rule: every arrow has the current view's name beside it.
- **The X doesn't say where it goes.** With the project hidden, the reader couldn't tell whether the X goes back to the project or to the project cards. In the app, the tooltip would say "Close and return to the project", but this check deliberately had no tooltips. The reader also guessed that the X throws away unsent text without asking. In fact the printer chat already asks before it closes.
- **"‹ Version history" still reads slightly as a destination.** The reader hesitated a little, though less than before. A wider gap between the chevron and the title is the untested fix.

The updated project screen is at /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/c12bc384-715f-4358-96e9-34fc4c43d898/scratchpad/nav/project-3.png.
Yes, update boards

content.text:
The canvas now uses the new back-and-close pattern everywhere it applies: https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ (version 185, labelled "Back and close: one navigation pattern"). I changed 82 boards in place, added one new board, and added a note that states the rule. Because I edited the old boards rather than drawing replacements, nothing needed marking as superseded.

**What changed on the boards:**
- **Project screens (65 boards):** "‹ Home" is now an outlined arrow button followed by the project name. The name is "Garage bracket", or "find_my_hollow" on the boards where the chat says find_my_hollow.3mf was opened.
- **Home (11 boards):** the header shows the JusPrin logo only, with no "› Home".
- **Print history (3 boards):** the back button is now the outlined arrow.
- **Chat header, which most AI-panel boards share:** the back control is a small chevron with no outline. Before, it was a chat-bubble icon on most screens and an outlined chevron on the header-states board.
- **Project tab, Details view:** "‹ Project" over "Details" became a single row, a chevron then "Details".
- **AI tool setup steps:** the chevron is its own button and the title sits beside it, so the title no longer reads as part of the link.
- **Printer panel sketch on the Agent setup page:** "‹ Back" became an X followed by "Add a printer".
- **New board on the Main Page:** the printer chat covering the whole window, with the X, "Add a printer", and "Browse the full printer list". Next to it is a note setting out the five rules.

I rendered seven boards from different groups and checked their headers. All of them drew correctly.

**What I deliberately left alone:**
- **Two Project tab boards** (26e3 and 26e4) draw "‹ Project" above the Project tab's first page. The app has no back row there, so those boards already disagree with the app. Whether to remove the row is your call.
- **Wizard steps:** the "Back" links on the first-launch steps move between steps of one flow, not between screens.
- **Header menus:** sub-lists keep their first row as the way back.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify the checked-in functional icons against an unpacked lucide-static release.

Usage: python3 verify_lucide.py /path/to/unpacked/lucide-static/package
"""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def main() -> int:
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print(__doc__.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    package = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
    manifest = json.loads((here / "lucide-map.json").read_text())
    package_manifest = json.loads((package / "package.json").read_text())
    expected = f"{manifest['package']}@{manifest['version']}"
    actual = f"{package_manifest['name']}@{package_manifest['version']}"
    if actual != expected:
        print(f"Expected {expected}, got {actual}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    mismatches = []
    known = set(manifest["icons"])
    for extra in sorted({path.stem for path in here.glob("*.svg")} - known):
        mismatches.append(f"{extra}.svg has no provenance mapping")
    for local, upstream in manifest["icons"].items():
        if (here / f"{local}.svg").read_bytes() != (package / "icons" / f"{upstream}.svg").read_bytes():
            mismatches.append(f"{local}.svg != {upstream}.svg")
    if (here / "LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt").read_bytes() != (package / "LICENSE").read_bytes():
        mismatches.append("LUCIDE-LICENSE.txt != LICENSE")
    if mismatches:
        print("\n".join(mismatches), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"Verified {len(manifest['icons'])} SVGs and license against {expected}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

It is shown only while the thread's bottom is out of view, with no label and no count, and pressing it scrolls to the bottom and follows again. The thread follows new content while the person is at the bottom, including when the composer grows; a scroll up holds the view, and answers and the app's own turns never move it; any message of the person's (typed, a reply choice, Ask AI) scrolls to the bottom and follows again.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the boards on the canvas's Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Agent-pane collapse: an icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.

metadata:

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].
