---
name: render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].

   - The pattern was agreed and drawn on the canvas earlier (canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ).

content.text:
The back and close controls are built and follow the pattern we agreed. Your answers needed two small canvas edits first. The project boards now show "Saved" after the project name, and the navigation note on the canvas lists the chat titles. Both went out as canvas version 186.

**What someone sees now**
- **Home:** the header shows only the logo and Preferences. There's no back control.
- **Project screen:** the header starts with an outlined arrow. Its tooltip says "Back to Home". After the arrow comes the project name, then its save state in grey ("Saved", "Saving…", or "Couldn't save" in red).
- **Print history:** the back control is the same outlined arrow. Its tooltip says "Back to Home" or "Back to the project", depending on where you came from.
- **Chats that fill the window:** they close with an outlined X, followed by a title. These are the titles I chose:
  - Adding a printer: "Add a printer".
  - Connecting one: "Connect Lab Printer", using the printer's name.
  - AI help with printer settings: "Lab Printer settings".
  - AI help with filament settings: "Bambu PLA Basic settings", using the filament's name.

  When the app knows where closing returns to, the X's tooltip names it, for example "Back to Prepare".
- **Panels:** going back inside a panel uses a quiet chevron with no outline, on the same row as the view's title. This covers the project pane's Details and Version history views, the all-settings view, and the setup screens. Before, Details and Version history used two rows.

**One thing I changed after looking at the real window**
The first capture showed a bug in my header code. In a 1200-point window with the AI panel open, the project name shrank to "2." and ran under the printer chip. I fixed it in two ways:
- The chip now sits midway between the name and the Slice button, as on the boards, instead of in the centre of the header.
- When space is short, the chip shrinks first, because the printer choice matters more than the name. The window's title bar also shows the name. The name always keeps at least a fifth of the free space. "Saved" is dropped when the name and the state don't both fit.

That priority is my call, not something you agreed to. In the 1200-point window the header now reads "← 20mmbox-LF | Bamb… · 0.4 · from the file". In a 1700-point window it shows everything, including "Saved". Both captures are attached.

**Tests**
- Agent page: 713 of 713 pass.
- Home page: 160 of 160 pass.
- Shell test harness: the main run passes with 626 checks and no failures, including the header layout checks, after the fix. The left-pane runs pass too.
- Print history harness: one check fails, `print_history_stopped_print_only_started`. It was already failing before this work. A commit on November 8 made Print history skip prints that neither finished nor are running, but the check still expects a "Started" row for one.

**Still open**
- The filament chat's header still has the button that hides the AI panel on its right, even though that chat fills the window. It was there before this change, and I left it alone.
- I didn't commit anything. The work is in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/nav-pattern` on branch `claude/nav-pattern`.
